author: JKawesome
body:
Hey guys! So while I was writing an XML to test out my map on a PGM server, I realized there are a few Overcast XML generators out there, but none for Avicus YML. So yesterday, I started developing a YML generator for Avicus. I've also recorded myself speedcoding it, so I'll update this thread each time I upload a speedcode video, and section that I've completed. 

The Goal

My goal for this project is to make an easy-to-use, user friendly YML generator that anyone will be able to use instantly. It features a drag and drop interface (suggested by ParaSpider), and users are able to drag modules onto the canvas, which would generate the code.

If you would like to contribute to making modules, please contact me on Skype. Thanks!

Speedcode Videos:

Day #1 - Basic layout; info and repair/remove drops sections.
http://youtu.be/1T80nZ8lCcA
Day #2 - Part one of the loadout module.
http://youtu.be/Nixrmj1WC9E
Day #3 - Part two of the loadout module, hopefully will be finished by tomorrow.
http://youtu.be/8Xu72w4txhA
Day #4 - Part three of the loadout module, as well as implementing a new design.
http://youtu.be/gGLFeXA8TAk
Day #5 - Finishing up the loadout module.
http://youtu.be/4CjHVmjMgkw
Day #6 - Fixing bugs on Github
http://youtu.be/jrYm8J1u4-c
Day #7 - Fixing more bugs, and starting drag-and-drop UI
http://youtu.be/5e-c9EcJAMs
Day #8 - Continuing the UI, and combing through bugs on Github.
http://youtu.be/HE63wyUz5Go

Also, note that I do work on this outside of videos, but I don't record it since I usually sit down for a short amount of time, not long enough for a recording, as videos are sped up 20x and usually take 2-3 hours to record.

Some Links:

If you find any issues/bugs while testing it, please report it here, and I'll get to it ASAP.
https://github.com/JKawesome/AvicusYML/issues

I do have a public beta, and it will be updated daily, along with the video releases. You're welcome to take a look at the beta here: www.avicusyml.com

I will not send you a download of the source code, since it's private and currently only maintained by me. However, if you really want to see the source, it's all online.

Gamemodes Currently Supported:

✔ Nexus

I came up with and implemented a new design today, and it features three columns, as opposed to the two column layout it had before.

The first column will be for users to search and browse through modules, or blocks, to add to the YML. There, they can select, for example, a region, and drag it into the middle column. The YML code output will automatically update on the third column. It's not completely finished yet, but I've pushed out what I have so far onto the beta site, if you want to see it.

replies.body:
I finally got the chance to record another speedcode video, and while it's processing, I'd like to update you guys on what's going on with this project. I finished the loadout module and combed out most of the known bugs. However, Enchanted Books will not be included inside the loadout, as IvyCode told me it isn't possible with Avicus's current YML. Direct quote from Ivy:

Hello,
Currently there is no way to achieve this. Perhaps an update would allow adding enchanted books to loadouts.
Sorry!

I also worked on the new interface, which, in my opinion, actually looks really cool and could be practical once complete. It features a drag-and-drop interface, where users could potentially grab any code block they need, and drag it into their project. It's a little hard to explain, but I just updated the beta website, so see for yourself!

Also, the new video will be available here once it finishes processing:

http://youtu.be/HE63wyUz5Go

replies.author: JKawesome
replies.body:
Biggest update so far since the release

Alright, I spent my entire weekend working on this, and honestly, I'm really satisfied with the outcome. Although I don't have a video, here are some of the key things that I did:

- New domain name (www.avicusyml.com)
- Finished draggable UI
- Re-coded everything into individual modules
- New web server (a lot of server-side issues fixed)
- Completed and polished existing modules

I know this doesn't seem like a lot, but it actually makes a huge difference. This means that I can start working on individual modules, hopefully starting with teams and objectives.

Also, this means that if anyone would like to contribute to making modules, it would be possible since they're all independent and won't cause any errors. If you have decent knowledge in HTML, Javascript/JQuery, and PHP, and would like to help, please contact me on Skype (JKPlaysMinecraft).

By the way, if you're testing this and run into bugs/issues, please, post it on Github, so I know about it and can fix it. Thanks!

replies.author: JKawesome
replies.body:
Basic Nexus Support

Alright, I just pushed the newest version onto the public beta server. I added support for teams, so it should support Nexus right now without any problems, at least meeting the minimum YML requirements. I've also added a menu that gives you templates of the modules required for the specific gamemodes. I'm working on a list of modules that I plan to develop, so I'll post that as soon as I'm done, and I'll check them off as I go along. But for now, if you have a nexus map waiting for a YML, here's your chance. I've attached a few screenshots of the new features.

Contribution

Also, again, as I've mentioned in the last thread, if you have some spare time and are proficient with HTML, CSS, and Javascript, and would like to contribute to making plugins, please contact me over Skype and we can discuss the details. Currently, Fluenza is helping me make a sexy new design, so a huge thanks to him!
